Three places in `PatientAllergyResource2_0` call `PatientService.getAllergies` directly. These are the only production callers I found in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, the module that serves the generic `/ws/rest/v1` resources. I ran one search for `getAllergies(` in that repository and read the resource file. I didn't check other modules, or whether anything reaches `getAllergies` indirectly. I read the file only up to line 289 of 315. The third caller (line 305) and its method boundaries come from the search result and the Javadoc, not from reading that code.

**Production code (`PatientAllergyResource2_0`)**
- `doGetAll` (line 169) serves `GET /patient/{uuid}/allergy`. It branches on the returned `Allergies` status. `UNKNOWN` throws `NoContentFoundException` (a 204 response). `NO_KNOWN_ALLERGIES` returns an empty list. `SEE_LIST` returns the allergies. A change to the returned status or contents would alter this endpoint directly.
- `delete(String parentUniqueId, String uuid, ...)` (line 222) serves `DELETE /patient/{uuid}/allergy`. It loads the allergies and voids each one to reset the patient to the unknown state. A changed result would change which allergies get voided.
- The `PUT /patient/{uuid}/allergy` method (line 305) reads the allergies and sets the allergy status, such as `NO_KNOWN_ALLERGIES`. Its Javadoc starts around line 285.

**Tests that would also be affected (`PatientAllergyController2_0Test`)**
- This test class calls `getAllergies` 13 times, at lines 93, 101, 151, 171, 182, 204, 215, 234, 264, 295, 301, 309, 320 and 352. It uses the calls to check the state left behind by the controller operations.
